sampling_model.design: A sampled panel \(\varnothing\neq S\in\mathcal P_k\) is chosen ex ante, with \(n_c\in\mathbb N_{>0}\) for every \(c\in S\) and \(\sum_{c\in S}n_c=N\); the \(N\) fixed units are assigned uniformly over the corresponding multi-arm partitions. The panel \(S=\varnothing\) is a separate deterministic population-width case with no assignment law.
sampling_model.units: The covariates \(x_i\) and full bounded potential-outcome schedules \(Y_i(a,t)\) are fixed; only assignment \(Z\) is random. The source-faithful finite-\(\Gamma\) formulation ranges over \(\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO},\Gamma}\); the aggregate class \(\mathcal M_N\) is a mean-level enlargement with exactly the same induced cell-mean surfaces, selected means, and policy values.
sampling_model.treatment: Assignment to arm \(c\) deploys the deterministic action \(c(x_i)\) at known score \(m_c\).
sampling_model.overlap: For sampled designs, \(S\neq\varnothing\), every selected arm has \(n_c\geq1\), and the in-scope arm counts sum to \(N\); no positive realized arm-by-cell count is required by the Horvitz--Thompson construction.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no estimated propensity. Simultaneous without-replacement bounds are constructed for the selected arm-cell means and propagated deterministically through the sharp endpoint maps.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Our bounds are tight, and cannot be improved without further assumptions.
The worst-case regret is approximately equal---and sometimes exactly equal---to the objective function of a k-median problem.
The certificate format is designed with simplicity in mind.
Our approach treats the ILP solver as a black-box oracle.
The proposed confidence intervals for all effect quantiles are simultaneously valid.
The empirical minimax regret estimator is computationally tractable and possesses favorable regret convergence properties.
Our approach relies on constructing averaging estimators where the weights are carefully adapted.
Probability inequalities are obtained for sums of bounded random variables.
There is a combinatorial \(O(\log m+\log k)\)-approximation algorithm for the robust \(k\)-median problem.
Greedily constructed maximum \(k\)-coverage solutions are guaranteed to be within a factor \(1-1/e\) of optimal.

body.tldr: One randomized panel of deterministic machine-learning policies must support sharp causal validation of a prespecified update library. The finite-\(\Gamma\) nearest-matching-score width is exact both for the aggregate cell-mean class and for a source-faithful individual-level Chen--Oberst subclass, because homogenization makes their induced mean surfaces coincide. Under the actual bounded no-Lipschitz Chen--Oberst class, the exact prospective cell cost is zero only for a selected matching neutral arm or a selected matching nonneutral arm at exactly the target score, and is one otherwise; homogeneous common endpoint schedules prove sharpness. The rational mixed-integer panel optimization and simultaneous assignment-only coverage remain supporting design and inference results.

project_justification.gap: ChenOberst2025 supplies tight monotonicity-only reusable-validation bounds under unit-level performance monotonicity and neutral-action equality, but not the finite-\(\Gamma\) prospective nearest-score panel identity. AnthonyGoyalGuptaNagarajan2010 supplies the robust scenario nearest-facility skeleton, MontielOleaPrallonQiuStoyeSun2025 supplies the closest causal \(k\)-median analogy, and HochbaumPathria1998 supplies the zero-sensitivity maximum-coverage boundary.
project_justification.niche: The field niche is the causal derivation of the exact design loss: a faithful bridge shows that the finite-\(\Gamma\) common-schedule and width results remain exact on an individual-level Chen--Oberst subclass, while a separate theorem recovers the genuine no-Lipschitz class with its exact binary matching geometry.
project_justification.fill: The project proves common sharp endpoint schedules and attained prospective causal-width identities for both regimes, a rational budget-optimal panel formulation, and simultaneous randomization-only outer coverage. The mixed-integer program, exhaustive branch certificate, maximum-coverage reduction, and explicit rational instance are implementation and falsification infrastructure rather than the field novelty.

body.related_work: Chen and Oberst (2025, Introduction, Section 4, Remark 3.1, and Appendix D.1) study reusable validation under bounded unit-level performance monotonicity and unit-level neutral-action equality, without a Lipschitz restriction, and prove tight bounds. The present conditional-mean monotonicity and neutral invariance are relaxations in aggregation, whereas finite \(\Gamma\)-Lipschitz smoothness is a refinement; the two unrestricted classes are incomparable. A homogenization bridge proves that the individual-level \(\Gamma\)-Lipschitz subclass and the aggregate class generate the same mean surfaces, and a separate no-Lipschitz theorem recovers the exact Chen--Oberst regime with binary exact-score or neutral matching costs. Anthony, Goyal, Gupta, and Nagarajan (2010, Section 2 and Theorem 2.2) supply the robust min-max \(k\)-median skeleton; the metric lift is informed by that result and does not claim its approximation theory. Montiel Olea, Prallon, Qiu, Stoye, and Sun (2025, Theorem 1 and Appendix A.2) connect causal site selection to \(k\)-median for a different estimand. Hochbaum and Pathria (1998) supply the maximum-\(k\)-coverage benchmark. Cheung, Gleixner, and Steffy (2017) and Szeider (2026) motivate exact rational proof logs. Caughey, Dafoe, Li, and Miratrix (2023) study finite-sample randomization-only simultaneous inference for a different causal family, while Hadad, Hirshberg, Zhan, Wager, and Athey (2021) study adaptive policy evaluation. Hoeffding (1963) supplies the sampling-without-replacement concentration comparison.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The common endpoint schedules establish simultaneous marginal lower and upper corners, not rectangularity of the full joint value set. The aggregate mean class and the no-Lipschitz individual-level class are not interchangeable: neither contains the other on nondegenerate populations. Exact score-distance gains require the finite-\(\Gamma\) subclass; monotonicity alone yields only binary exact-score or neutral-action protection. The facility-location lift does not transfer a published approximation ratio to every implementation convention. The exhaustive certificate can be exponential, and the outer confidence intervals are conservative rather than shortest. Scores, libraries, \(\Gamma\), and the budget are fixed before assignment.
body.honest_scope: The field obligations are the common causal endpoint schedules, the exact prospective widths derived from observationally indistinguishable fixed arrays, the faithful bridge to the individual-level Chen--Oberst class, and simultaneous assignment-only coverage. The finite-\(\Gamma\) identity is exact on the individual-level Lipschitz subclass and on the larger aggregate mean class because their induced mean surfaces coincide; it is not attributed to the published no-Lipschitz assumptions. For that actual no-Lipschitz class, the proved prospective cost is binary. The project does not claim a rectangular joint value set, optimize allocation, estimate future scores, or supply a polynomial exact algorithm on unrestricted instances.
